questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding the Constitutional body and its Nodal Ministry?

options.text: Inter State Council - Ministry of Finance
Attorney general of India - Ministry of Home Affairs
National Commission for SCs - Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Union Public Service Commission - Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Public Service Commission - Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is a Constitutional body responsible for conducting prestigious exams like Civil Services Examination, Indian Forest Service Examination, and others.
 
• It is under the **administrative control of the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**, which is headed by the Prime Minister as the Minister-in-charge.
 
• The Ministry provides **administrative support and resources** to UPSC for its functioning.
 
• UPSC was established under **Article 315** of the Indian Constitution, which provides for its composition, appointment, and tenure of members.
 
• The body is independent and insulated from external pressures, ensuring **fair and transparent recruitment** to various government posts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter State Council**

 
 
• The Inter State Council is a Constitutional body established under **Article 263** of the Constitution to facilitate coordination between the Union and State governments.
 
• It is under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not the Ministry of Finance.
 
• The Council is primarily tasked with addressing disputes and fostering cooperative federalism in India.
 
 
 
• **Attorney General of India**
 
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer of India, appointed under **Article 76** of the Constitution.
 
• He/She is not linked to the Ministry of Home Affairs but works as the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• The Attorney General is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)**
 
 
• The NCSC is a Constitutional body established under **Article 338** of the Constitution.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**, not the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
 
• The Commission safeguards the interests of Scheduled Castes and investigates complaints regarding their rights and privileges.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**
 
 
• This Ministry is the **nodal ministry** for personnel management, including recruitment, training, and capacity building in the Government of India.
 
• It oversees the functioning of Constitutional bodies like UPSC and statutory bodies like the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC).
 
• The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) is a key department under this Ministry.

questions.question: When did the Prime Minister of India launch 'Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**October 2024**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan' was launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi in October 2024**.
 
• The initiative aims to drive **socio-economic development in tribal areas** with a focus on sustainable growth and self-reliance.
 
• This program aligns with the Indian government’s ongoing efforts to strengthen **tribal welfare and empowerment** under various schemes.
 
• The campaign is named after the revered tribal leader **Birsa Munda**, often referred to as 'Dharti Aaba'.
 
• The Abhiyan emphasizes **education, skill development, health, and livelihood opportunities** for tribal communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Birsa Munda**

 
 
• Birsa Munda was a freedom fighter, religious leader, and folk hero who belonged to the Munda tribe in Jharkhand.
 
• He played a significant role in mobilizing tribal communities against British colonial rule.
 
• Birsa Munda is remembered for his efforts to protect tribal land and culture.
 
• He is referred to as 'Dharti Aaba', meaning 'Father of the Earth'.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Welfare in India**
 
 
• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is responsible for the implementation of various schemes targeting tribal communities.
 
• Key schemes include **Vanbandhu Kalyan Yojana**, **Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana**, and **Eklavya Model Residential Schools**.
 
• These programs focus on providing education, healthcare, and livelihood opportunities to tribal populations.
 
 
 
• **Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS)**
 
 
• EMRS aims to impart quality education to tribal children in remote areas.
 
• The schools provide free education, accommodation, and meals to students.
 
• The curriculum emphasizes both academics and extracurricular activities to ensure holistic development.
 
 
 
• **Van Dhan Yojana**
 
 
• Van Dhan Yojana is an initiative under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to promote tribal entrepreneurship.
 
• It focuses on the value addition of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) through self-help groups.
 
• The scheme aims to enhance the income of tribal communities by leveraging their traditional knowledge and resources.

questions.question: Which term is used to describe the area of land that drains into a particular river or lake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Watershed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **watershed** is an area of land where all the water drains into a particular river, lake, or other water body.
 
• It includes both surface water (streams, rivers, lakes) and groundwater that flows into the water system.
 
• Watersheds are usually separated by geographical features such as ridges, hills, or mountains.
 
• They play a critical role in water cycle management by collecting, storing, and channeling rainfall and snowmelt to downstream water bodies.
 
• Watershed management is essential for ensuring water quality, preventing floods, and sustaining biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delta**

 
 
• A delta is a landform created at the mouth of a river where it deposits sediments as it flows into a slower-moving or stagnant water body like an ocean, sea, or lake.
 
• Examples include the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta and the Nile Delta.
 
 
 
• **Estuary**
 
 
• An estuary is a coastal area where freshwater from rivers meets and mixes with saltwater from the ocean.
 
• Estuaries are rich in biodiversity and serve as crucial habitats for many aquatic species.
 
 
 
• **Reservoir**
 
 
• A reservoir is an artificial or natural lake used to store water for various purposes such as irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• Examples include the Hirakud Reservoir in India and Lake Mead in the United States.
 
 
 
• **Watershed Management**
 
 
• Watershed management involves sustainable practices to conserve water, prevent erosion, and protect the ecosystem in a watershed area.
 
• It includes activities like afforestation, soil conservation, and rainwater harvesting.

questions.question: Through which Amendment of the Indian Constitution was the Right to Education designated as a Fundamental Right?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **86th Amendment Act**, enacted in 2002, inserted **Article 21A** into the Indian Constitution, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right.
 
• It mandates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• To operationalize this, the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE Act)** was passed in 2009 and came into effect on April 1, 2010.
 
• The amendment also modified **Article 45**, obligating the State to provide early childhood care and education to children below six years of age.
 
• Additionally, it inserted **Article 51A(k)**, specifying that parents or guardians must provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**:

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, ensuring basic rights to all citizens.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts and protect citizens from arbitrary actions by the State.
 
• Articles 12 to 35 cover various Fundamental Rights, including the right to equality, freedom, and education.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A**:
 
 
• Introduced by the 86th Amendment, Article 21A provides the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right.
 
• This article ensures that every child aged 6 to 14 years has access to free and compulsory education.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**:
 
 
• The RTE Act is a legislative framework to implement the provisions of Article 21A.
 
• It specifies the responsibilities of the central and state governments, schools, and parents in ensuring universal education.
 
• It also mandates a 25% reservation for economically weaker sections in private schools.
 
 
 
• **Early Childhood Care and Education**:
 
 
• Article 45, as amended, emphasizes the importance of pre-primary education for children below six years of age.
 
• Programs like **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)** aim to cater to this need.

• It was introduced in the inaugural season of IPL in 2008.
 
• The cap is passed on from one bowler to another during the season, depending on who tops the wicket-taker list.
 
• At the end of the tournament, the highest wicket-taker retains the Purple Cap.

• They won the IPL title in their inaugural season under the leadership of Hardik Pandya.

• The tournament featured 10 teams and was played across various venues in India.
 
• The Chennai Super Kings defeated the Gujarat Titans in the final to win their 5th IPL title.

questions.question: Which member of the phylum Porifera is the oldest metazoan group still existing on our planet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sponges**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sponges (phylum Porifera) are considered the **oldest metazoan group** still existing on Earth, dating back to the Precambrian era, approximately 600 million years ago.
 
• They are simple multicellular organisms that lack tissues, organs, and a nervous system but possess specialized cells for various functions like feeding and reproduction.
 
• Sponges rely on a water canal system to filter feed, making them highly efficient filter feeders in aquatic ecosystems.
 
• Their fossil records suggest that they played a significant role in the evolution of early marine ecosystems and are considered a cornerstone in the study of evolutionary biology.
 
• Sponges are exclusively aquatic, with the majority being marine, although some freshwater species also exist.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Porifera:**

 
 
• Porifera, commonly known as sponges, derive their name from the Latin word "porus" (pore) and "ferre" (to bear), referring to their porous bodies.
 
• They exhibit **asymmetrical or radial symmetry** and are sessile as adults.
 
• Sponges have a skeleton made of spicules (calcareous or siliceous) or spongin fibers, providing structural support.
 
 
 
• **Water Canal System:**
 
 
• Sponges use a specialized canal system comprising ostia (pores), spongocoel (central cavity), and osculum (excurrent opening) to circulate water for feeding, respiration, and excretion.
 
• This system is driven by the beating of flagella in specialized cells called choanocytes.
 
 
 
• **Reproductive Strategies:**
 
 
• Sponges reproduce both sexually (via gametes) and asexually (budding, fragmentation, or gemmules).
 
• They are hermaphroditic, meaning an individual can produce both eggs and sperm, although cross-fertilization is common.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Sponges serve as habitat-forming species, providing shelter for various marine organisms.
 
• They play a crucial role in nutrient cycling by filtering large volumes of water and capturing microscopic particles.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Significance:**
 
 
• Sponges are considered basal metazoans, representing an evolutionary link between unicellular and multicellular life forms.
 
• They offer insights into the origin and evolution of multicellular animals due to their simple body structure and cellular organization.

questions.question: The period when we find environmental changes, beginning about 12,000 years ago till about 10,000 years ago, is called:

__
 
• The Mesolithic period, also known as the **Middle Stone Age**, spanned roughly from 12,000 to 10,000 years ago.
 
• This period marks the transition between the Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) and Neolithic (New Stone Age) periods.
 
• It was characterized by significant **environmental changes** due to the end of the last Ice Age, leading to a warmer climate.
 
• Humans in the Mesolithic period began using more sophisticated tools, known as **microliths**, which were small, sharp stone tools.
 
• During this time, people adopted a **semi-nomadic lifestyle**, combining hunting, fishing, and gathering with early forms of agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palaeolithic Period:**

 
 
• The Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) lasted from about 2.5 million years ago to around 10,000 BCE.
 
• Humans were hunter-gatherers during this period and used rudimentary tools made of stone.
 
• Cave paintings and other forms of early art emerged during the late Palaeolithic.
 
 
 
• **Microliths:**
 
 
• Microliths were small, geometrically shaped stone tools used during the Mesolithic period.
 
• These tools were often attached to wooden or bone handles to create arrows, spears, and other composite tools.
 
 
 
• **Neolithic Period:**
 
 
• The Neolithic period (New Stone Age) followed the Mesolithic, beginning around 10,000 BCE.
 
• It was marked by the advent of agriculture, domestication of animals, and permanent settlements.
 
• Humans began using polished stone tools and developed pottery and weaving techniques.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Changes:**
 
 
• The end of the Ice Age led to warmer climates, rising sea levels, and the formation of new ecosystems.
 
• These changes influenced the availability of plants and animals, prompting humans to adapt their subsistence strategies.

questions.question: 4In the context of Keynesian economics, what would be an ideal government response to an overheated economy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Implement contractionary fiscal policies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Contractionary fiscal policies involve reducing government spending or increasing taxes to curb excessive demand in the economy.
 
• These policies aim to slow down inflationary pressures in an overheated economy by reducing aggregate demand.
 
• Increased taxes reduce disposable income, discouraging consumer spending and cooling down demand-driven inflation.
 
• Lower government spending reduces the injection of money into the economy, thereby controlling inflation and stabilizing the economic cycle.
 
• Such measures help achieve a sustainable growth rate while maintaining price stability and avoiding economic disruptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keynesian Economics:**

 
 
• Developed by economist John Maynard Keynes, this framework emphasizes the role of aggregate demand in driving economic output.
 
• It advocates government intervention in managing economic cycles to mitigate recessions and overheating.
 
 
 
• **Overheated Economy:**
 
 
• An economic condition characterized by high inflation, excessive demand, and unsustainable growth rates.
 
• Indicators include rising prices, labor shortages, and pressure on production capacities.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Control Measures:**
 
 
• Besides fiscal policy, monetary tools like increasing interest rates are used to combat inflation.
 
• Central banks play a critical role in implementing monetary policies to complement fiscal efforts.
 
 
 
• **Aggregate Demand:**
 
 
• The total demand for goods and services in an economy at a given time and price level.
 
• It is influenced by factors such as consumer spending, investment, government spending, and net exports.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the British government publish the White Paper based on the recommendations of the Third Round Table Conference?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The British government published the **White Paper** in 1933 based on the recommendations of the **Third Round Table Conference**.
 
• The White Paper served as the basis for the **Government of India Act, 1935**, which aimed to introduce provincial autonomy and reforms in British India's governance system.
 
• The **Third Round Table Conference** was held in London from November 1932 to December 1932, focusing on constitutional reforms for India.
 
• Unlike the previous conferences, the **Third Round Table Conference** saw limited participation from Indian political leaders and focused heavily on British perspectives.
 
• The White Paper outlined proposals for reforms, but it faced criticism from Indian leaders who viewed it as inadequate and biased toward British interests.

• Three Round Table Conferences were held between 1930 and 1932 to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
 
• The **First Round Table Conference (1930)** saw participation from British officials, Indian princes, and other representatives, but no Congress leaders attended.
 
• The **Second Round Table Conference (1931)** included Mahatma Gandhi as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The **Third Round Table Conference (1932)** had fewer Indian representatives and was largely dominated by British officials.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• It was based on the recommendations of the White Paper published in 1933.
 
• The act introduced provincial autonomy and a federal structure for governance.
 
• It marked a significant step toward self-governance but was criticized for retaining excessive power in British hands.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the White Paper**
 
 
• The White Paper was criticized for failing to address India's demand for complete independence.
 
• It led to further alienation of Indian political leaders, particularly the Indian National Congress.
 
• It served as a precursor to the Government of India Act, 1935, which became the framework for British India's governance until independence.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures in the Round Table Conferences**
 
 
• British Prime Ministers **Ramsay MacDonald** and **Stanley Baldwin** played pivotal roles in hosting and moderating the conferences.
 
• Indian representatives included leaders from various communities, such as **B.R. Ambedkar**, **Tej Bahadur Sapru**, and **Sir Muhammad Iqbal**.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's participation in the Second Round Table Conference was a notable event, focusing on India's demand for independence.

questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 11, 6, 55 and 9 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the options using divisibility rules for the given numbers (11, 6, 55, 9).

For a number to be divisible by 55, it must end in 0 or 5. Options 921 and 1032 are instantly eliminated.

For a number to be divisible by 9, the sum of its digits must be a multiple of 9.

The sum of digits of 990 is 18 (divisible by 9), while for 1054 it is 10 (not divisible by 9).

Thus, 990 is the only option that satisfies all divisibility conditions.

**∴ The correct answer is 990.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 11, 6, 55, and 9.

**Formula Used:**

The smallest number completely divisible by a given set of numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 11 = 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 55 = 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 9 = 3 × 3 = 3²

⇒ LCM = Product of the highest powers of all involved prime factors

⇒ LCM = 2¹ × 3² × 5¹ × 11¹

⇒ LCM = 2 × 9 × 5 × 11

⇒ LCM = 10 × 99

⇒ LCM = 990

**∴ The correct answer is 990.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is found by taking the product of the highest powers of all prime factors present in the numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without leaving a remainder. It is found by taking the product of the lowest powers of only the common prime factors.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits results in a value that is a multiple of 9.
</p

questions.question: A man goes to Jaipur from Surat at a speed of 3km/hr and returns to Surat at speed of 15km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When equal distances are covered at two different speeds x and y, the Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Here, the going speed x = 3 km/hr and returning speed y = 15 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 3 × 15) ÷ (3 + 15)

Average Speed = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Surat to Jaipur (v₁) = 3 km/hr

Speed from Jaipur to Surat (v₂) = 15 km/hr

Let the one-way distance between Surat and Jaipur be D km.

 
 
 Surat

 
 Jaipur

 
 
• 
 Distance = D

 
 

 

 Speed = 3 km/hr

 
 

 

 Speed = 15 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D (Surat to Jaipur) + D (Jaipur to Surat) = 2D

⇒ Time taken to reach Jaipur (t₁) = D ÷ 3

⇒ Time taken to return to Surat (t₂) = D ÷ 15

⇒ Total Time = (D ÷ 3) + (D ÷ 15)

⇒ Taking LCM of 3 and 15, Total Time = (5D + D) ÷ 15

⇒ Total Time = 6D ÷ 15 = 2D ÷ 5

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (2D ÷ 5)

⇒ Average Speed = (2D × 5) ÷ 2D = 5 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

When unequal distances d₁, d₂, d₃ are covered at variable speeds, the core formula remains: Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂ + d₃) ÷ (t₁ + t₂ + t₃).

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered sequentially at speeds x, y and z, Average Speed = (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |x − y|. If they move towards each other in opposite directions, Relative Speed = x + y.

questions.question: P and Q can complete a piece of work in 28 days and 35 days, respectively. P begins to do the work and they work alternatively one at a time for one day each. In how many days will the whole work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(28, 35) = 140 units.

Efficiency: P = 5, Q = 4. Combined work in 2 days (1 cycle) = 9 units.

15 full cycles (30 days) work = 15 × 9 = 135 units.

Remaining 5 units will be done by P on the 31st day in exactly 1 day.

Total time = 30 + 1 = 31 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 31 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 28 days

Time taken by Q to complete the work = 35 days

P begins the work, and they work on alternate days.

**Concept Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Total Work = LCM of given days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P
 28
 140
 5
 
 

 Q
 35
 4
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in 1st day by P = 5 units

⇒ Work done in 2nd day by Q = 4 units

⇒ Total work done in 2 days = 5 + 4 = 9 units

⇒ Number of such complete 2-day cycles possible for 140 units = 140 ÷ 9 = 15 cycles

⇒ Work done in 15 cycles (15 × 2 = 30 days) = 15 × 9 = 135 units

⇒ Remaining work = 140 − 135 = 5 units

⇒ On the 31st day, it is P's turn again. P can do 5 units of work per day.

⇒ Time taken by P to complete the remaining 5 units = 5 ÷ 5 = 1 day

⇒ Total time taken to complete the whole work = 30 + 1 = 31 days

**∴ The correct answer is 31 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
